articles.title: Cameron Green injury opens door to Nic Maddinson ahead of first South Africa Test
articles.summary: Australia all-rounder fails to overcome abdominal strain. Maddinson or Cooper Connolly to fill No 5 spot in Durban opener. Andrew McDonald insists Nic Maddinson’s Test squad call-up should be no shock, with the left-hander edging closer to replacing the injured Cameron Green in Durban.
body: Green has been officially ruled out of Australia’s side for the opening Test against South Africa, after failing to overcome the abdominal strain suffered in last week’s final ODI.
Australia are confident the allrounder will return in the three-Test series, but do not expect to have him bowling given he was also managing a shoulder issue.
That has left the tourists with a call to make between Maddinson and Cooper Connolly, with a dry Kingsmead pitch ahead of Friday a major consideration.
Maddinson’s Test squad call up following a one-day cup century and Josh Inglis’s fractured finger was a feelgood story, given he beat testicular cancer last year.

articles.title: Midfield options and a fab front four - what we've learned about England
articles.summary: From Trent Alexander-Arnold's return to Alex Scott's debut, Phil McNulty assesses what England have learned during this international window.
body: England's World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina felt like the most painful wound of all as the so-called years of hurt stretched to six decades - but the process of recovery has started swiftly.

The extended international break and four Nations League games have afforded head coach Thomas Tuchel, so heavily criticised for his defensive tactics in that defeat in Atlanta, the opportunity to rebuild and rehabilitate from that disappointment.

Tuchel's squad included players recalled after being excluded from his plans and others who were new to the England fold, while mainstays like captain Harry Kane continued as the centrepiece of his plans.
So what has Tuchel learned from the start to England's Nations League campaign?

articles.title: Jude Bellingham hails 125-cap Harry Kane as England’s best-ever player
articles.summary: Captain scores twice in 3-0 win over Czechia. Kane equals Peter Shilton’s appearance record. Jude Bellingham called Harry Kane England’s best-ever player after the captain equalled Peter Shilton’s record of 125 caps during Tuesday’s 3-0 win over Czechia in the Nations League.
body: Kane, who is only nine off a century of international goals after scoring twice in another fine display, was the star attraction as the Wembley crowd watched Thomas Tuchel’s side close on a spot in March’s quarter-finals. England’s record goalscorer showed why he is in the running for the Ballon d’Or and the way the Bayern Munich striker passed another milestone earned him rave reviews from Bellingham.
“There’s not much more you can say that hasn’t already been said,” the midfielder said. “From my perspective first and foremost he is an unbelievable human being, as a captain and a man.

“He is the best England player to ever wear the shirt and it is an honour to play with him. He is pretty unmatched. He is scoring goals for fun, he goes deep and he gets tackles in. He is only getting better.”

Kane, who made the opening goal when he crossed for Czechia’s Vladimir Coufal to put into his own net, said making his 125th appearance for his country goes down as one of the biggest achievements of his career.

articles.title: Harry Kane doubles up on landmark night as England cruise past Czechia
articles.summary: It was a night that belonged to Harry Kane. Yet another one. It began with him being shown a replay of his first England goal during a pre-match interview with ITV – the header against Lithuania in 2015, just 79 seconds after he came on as a substitute for his debut.
body: It remains a numbers game for Kane. They are getting bigger and ever more impressive. On the occasion of his 125th cap, the one that took him level with Peter Shilton at the top of the all-time England list, he moved to an astonishing 91 goals. Nobody will be surprised if he reaches the century. The only question appears to be when.

England know how to beat the game’s smaller fry. Under Thomas Tuchel, they have played 16 matches against teams ranked outside the world’s top 20. They have won 15 and drawn one – against Ghana at the World Cup. They have conceded only once – against the Democratic Republic of the Congo, also at the World Cup. Czechia, who are ranked No 50, were never in the contest.

Kane is similarly inevitable. The captain even claimed the assist for the breakthrough goal with a cross into the corridor of uncertainty that spooked Vladimir Coufal so severely he shot into his own net. Kane’s passing was very good. When he was withdrawn in the 82nd minute, he left to a great ovation.

articles.title: Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli is left with questions to answer after an inert Scotland performance leaves him still searching for his first home win, writes Tom English.
body: On a dismal night at Hampden when Scotland failed to ask enough questions of Slovenia, there are one or two that could be posed to new boss Sebastien Pocognoli and his players.

We knew Pocognoli was a disciple of three at the back - the issue being whether he was rigid or flexible in his philosophy, whether he was a bit of an ideologue or a coach capable of changing things on the hoof.

Well, he changed it, that's for sure. Maybe not early as he should have, but at 1-1, and then when Slovenia took a deserved 2-1 lead, Pocognoli switched formation and personnel, not out of design but out of desperation, you felt.
He hurled players on in a bid to take a point; strikers, wingers, kitchen-sink stuff. Indiscriminate and messy. Scotland never really got out of the blocks. They got what they deserved.

articles.title: Ronaldo wants Portugal 'punishment' but not retiring
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo says he is not retiring from international football but deserves to be punished for walking out on Portugal after head coach Jorge Jesus "broke his word to me".
body: The 41-year-old captain left his country's Nations League camp last week after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark.
Al-Nassr forward Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the Nations League twice.
In a lengthy statement, external, which ran to nearly 2,000 words, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United player said he should be held accountable for his actions.

But he accused Jesus of an "absolute breach of trust" for firstly not playing him against Norway after saying he would, before going back on a decision to present an agreed version of events to the media.

articles.title: U.S. Team Claims First-Ever FIM Enduro Vintage Trophy Victory
articles.summary: Fred Hoess, Billy Burns and Terry Cunningham win the Vintage Veterans Trophy at the 10th edition of the event. Photo credit: FIM/Future7Media. The FIM Enduro Vintage Trophy brings national teams together to race vintage enduro machines in a multi-day test of endurance, skill, and preparation.
body: The United States has won the FIM Enduro Vintage Trophy (EVT) for the first time. The American trio of Fred Hoess (Husqvarna), Billy Burns (Can-Am) and AMA Motorcycle Hall of Famer Terry Cunningham (Husqvarna) took the Vintage Veterans Trophy at the tenth running of the event in Zschopau, Germany.

"This is a proud moment for American motorcycling," said AMA President and CEO Rob Dingman. "Fred, Billy and Terry have given the United States its first-ever win at the FIM Enduro Vintage Trophy, and they did it against the best vintage riders in the world. Their win shows what's possible when passion, preparation and a love for these machines come together. On behalf of the AMA and our members, congratulations to the entire team."
Hoess also won the Final Cross Test in the Vintage Veterans Trophy individual classification. He finished ahead of Bernhard Walzer (KTM) of Austria and Italy's Tullio Pellegrinelli (Puch-Frigerio).

articles.title: UTSA-USF football: How to watch Roadrunners' showdown in national spotlight
articles.summary: Now in his seventh year leading UTSA, coach Jeff Traylor still doesn't believe the story behind the rise of Roadrunners football is talked about as much as it should be.
body: A program in just its 16th season has already reached the heights of Conference USA championships in 2021 and 2022, earning a jump to the American Conference in 2023. UTSA has finished with a winning record in every season of Traylor's tenure, establishing the Alamodome as perhaps the toughest environment in the Group of Six by going 35-5 at home through his tenure.

UTSA will have the rare opportunity to share its story with a broader audience this week, hosting SportsCenter in San Antonio before playing in an ESPN spotlight against South Florida at 6:30 p.m. Thursday in the Alamodome.
"It's on national TV, so it's got all the stuff that makes it a big game," Traylor said. "I think both of these teams will be in the hunt all the way to the end."
Traylor spoke to the Roadrunners this week about the eyes on the program and the chance to promote UTSA's brand, but he noted that they don't need much reminding.

articles.title: NLDS Game 3 Discussion: Milwaukee Brewers (2-0) @ San Diego Padres (0-2)
articles.summary: After a drama-filled win in Game 1 and a thrilling comeback win in Game 2, the Milwaukee Brewers are now looking to finish off a sweep of the San Diego Padres in the NLDS here in Game 3. To get there, Milwaukee sends right-hander Dustin May to the mound.
body: For San Diego, right-hander Nick Pivetta will get the ball. Pivetta, 33, finished sixth in NL Cy Young voting a year ago, and he pitched even better this season, though he was limited to just eight starts due to injury. In those outings, he totaled 34 2/3 innings with a 2.86 ERA, 2.21 FIP, and 42 strikeouts, and the Padres have won six of those eight games, including all four he made after his return in September. The 10-year veteran has made five career starts against Milwaukee with very rough results, going 1-3 with an 8.76 ERA and 24 strikeouts across 24 2/3 innings.

The star of Sunday’s game, Jackson Chourio bats in the leadoff spot and starts in left. He’s followed by Jake Bauers and William Contreras, with Brice Turang moving down to bat in the cleanup spot. Christian Yelich bats fifth as the DH, with Garrett Mitchell, Cooper Pratt, Sal Frelick, and Joey Ortiz rounding things out behind May.
First pitch in this one is at 8:38 p.m. CT on FS1 and the Brewers Radio Network.

articles.title: Kane sums up England legacy on special night - but can he make that final step?
articles.summary: Some things are inevitable in life. Harry Kane delivering for England is always one of those inevitabilities. On his momentous, milestone match, he stuck to the script perfectly.
body: On his 125th cap, Kane did what Kane does best under the Wembley arch - stealing the show, leading the way, winning the game for England.
Everyone knew he would score in this match. It's the same feeling you get in every match. But he still gets the buzz.
"I think this is even beyond my wildest dreams," he said after the game. "To be now at 125, it's just an extreme privilege."
This match - and the three goals he contributed to England's cause on his special night - was a perfect summary of Harry Kane's England career.

articles.title: Albany Academy wins Section 2 girls' golf team championship
articles.summary: Albany Academy's foursome of Sophia Kotlow, Sophia Brooks, Alexis Palmeri and Annabel Conway combined for a score of 344 (56-over par) on Tuesday at Eagle Crest Golf Club.
body: CLIFTON PARK - A chilly, windy morning gave way to clear skies and more comfortable conditions that made it smooth sailing for the Albany Academy girls' golf team to reclaim the Section 2 championship for the first time since 2023.
"It means a lot to do it as a team. All of us really put in the effort," said Sophia Kotlow, who posted the team's low score of the day with a 7-over 79. "No one (was) carried, no one dragged."
"We have such a great group of girls," said Caren Kotlow, who coaches Albany Academy alongside Karen Sbuttoni. "From eighth grade to seniors, they're such a cohesive group."
Shenendehowa, Shaker and Berne-Knox-Westerlo were the other competitors in the team event.

articles.title: Ronaldo breaks silence over Portugal walkout in extraordinary statement
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has broken his silence over his Portugal walkout in a lengthy statement in which he says he is not retiring from the national team.
body: The 41-year-old, whose actions had raised doubts over his international future, accused Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises in a near 2,000-word statement to his 679 million Instagram followers.

Addressing the uncertainty over his Portugal future, the Al Nassr forward said: "If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team."
Portugal boss Jesus, who previously denied there was a rift between him and his captain, said on Sunday the door was still open for Ronaldo to return to the national team.

However, the future of Portugal's record goalscorer and appearance-maker, whose 146 goals in 234 international caps is the most of any men's player in history, is far from clear following his decision to air his grievances in public.

articles.title: FIA directives questioned after formation lap 'farce' at Bahrain GP
articles.summary: David Croft has questioned the FIA after the chaotic formation lap scenes at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, describing a software glitch that saw several drivers slowing to a crawl or stopping completely as a "farce".
body: F1 and the FIA have new technical regulations this year which saw the introduction of a new power unit which is almost 50 per cent electric.

Sepang saw the first wet conditions of the season, and the FIA later confirmed that a combination of low engine speeds, low grip, wet-weather energy-management settings and the configuration of the circuit had caused an unintended loss of power.
Speaking on the F1 Show podcast, Sky Sports F1 commentator Croft questioned why such a scenario had not been simulated before the season began.
"We had a shakedown in Barcelona and six days of testing in Bahrain before the season started. Why on earth were situations like this not tried out before we went racing?" he said.
